title: pendingReward view does not clamp against balance and does not project dispatcher mintDebt, desynchronising UI display from claim behaviour under the new _safePay revert semantics
regression-risk: pre-existing (prior CS-07), now amplified by story-002 _safePay revert
description:
`pendingReward(address)` returns `(user.amount * acc) / ACC_PRECISION - user.rewardDebt` without clamping against `rewardToken.balanceOf(this)`, and without projecting outstanding `dispatcherHook.mintDebt()` into `accRewardPerShare`. Under the story-002 revert-on-shortfall change, a UI or keeper that reads `pendingReward()` and then calls `claim()` will see the transaction REVERT on the balance check, with no indication of what was actually claimable.

The view can simultaneously over-report (ignoring balance cap) and under-report (ignoring pending hook debt) — a confusing combination for integrators.
impact: Frontends and keepers display inaccurate figures and issue claim transactions that revert in shortfall conditions, wasting gas and producing poor UX. Automated claim bots can enter failed retry loops. Not a direct loss-of-funds issue.
proof: Read line 339. No balance clamp. `acc` computed in lines 331-338 does not fold in `dispatcherHook.mintDebt()`. Call `pendingReward(user)` in a state where contract balance < entitlement and then `claim()` — tx reverts in `_safePay` while the view promised the full entitlement.
suggested-fix: (a) Add a balance clamp: `return min(entitlement, rewardToken.balanceOf(this))`. (b) Optionally project the pending dispatcher mint-debt into `acc` before computing entitlement, giving a forward-looking view of what a sync-plus-claim would yield. Document the semantics clearly in NatSpec.
consolidation-note: No direct ES overlap (ES-04 concerns setWindowDuration rate mismatch, not pendingReward view). Standalone.
